stem.en: A speaker on the stage of a large hall plays one short note, then stops. Half a second later you still hear the note, from all directions, more softly. Why?

text.en: The walls store the sound and let it out slowly.
People in the audience repeat the note.
Many reflections from the walls, ceiling and floor reach you less than 0.05 s apart, so the sound goes on after the source stops.
The sound slows down inside the hall.

explanation.en: The walls, ceiling and floor reflect the note many times. The reflections reach you very close together, less than 0.05 s apart, so you hear one sound that goes on after the speaker stops. This is reverberation.

hints.en: What do the walls, ceiling and floor do to sound?
This lesson has a name for sound that goes on because of many reflections.
